title: How Quickly Can I Become a Medical Assistant?
summary: If you're looking for a fast path into healthcare, becoming a medical assistant can be a great option.
body_markdown:
If you're looking for a fast path into healthcare, becoming a medical assistant can be a great option. Rather than spending years in school, many programs provide the training you need in about nine months, helping you begin your career in less than a year. Find out[what to look for in a medical assistant school](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/health-sciences/medical-assistant/look-for-medical-assistant-school) , how programs enroll, and how long yours might take.


## How Long Does It Take to Become a Medical Assistant?


There is no single timeline for becoming a Medical Assistant. How long your training takes depends on your program, credential, attendance plan, and your school and state requirements. A medical assistant program can take from 35 weeks to more than two years. But if you want to get to work sooner, there are 7 steps you can take:


### 1. Make Sure Your Training Meets Your State’s Requirements


Before you choose your medical assistant program based on its speed, make sure it prepares you with the education and credentials you may need where you plan to work. Medical assistant requirements can vary by state, and certain duties may have additional training, certification, or credentialing requirements.


Research your state's requirements before you enroll and ask prospective schools how their program aligns with them. Also consider the requirements of healthcare employers in your area. Even when a particular certification isn't required by the state, employers may prefer or require candidates to hold one.


The right program should help you understand which credentials you may be eligible to pursue after graduation and whether its curriculum prepares you for applicable certification exams. Choosing the appropriate training from the beginning can help you avoid having to complete additional education or training later—and keep you on the most direct path toward your new career.


### 2. Choose a Medical Assistant School with Frequent Starts


The more quickly you get into school, the more quickly you can get out and into a medical assistant career. As you compare medical assistant schools, ask how frequently new classes start. Some colleges operate around traditional fall and spring semesters. Career schools, on the other hand, often have multiple start dates throughout the year.


A more flexible start schedule can help you avoid an unnecessary delay between deciding you want a new career and actually beginning your training.


### 3. Consider a Diploma Program Instead of a Two-Year Degree


You don't necessarily need an associate degree to pursue a career as a medical assistant. While a two-year degree may make sense if you’re thinking about long-term educational goals and the pursuit of a bachelor’s degree someday, you don’t need it to being your medical assistant career.


A career-focused diploma program takes a different approach. You concentrate your education on what you need for your medical assisting career. You get the knowledge, training, and hands-on experience, and then you can quickly apply for your first job in your new career. A diploma program doesn’t mean you can’t later pursue a more advanced degree. It just means you won’t do it today.


Before you enroll, ask what credential you'll earn, how long the program takes, what the program teaches, and whether it prepares you for the type of medical assistant opportunities you want to pursue.


### 4. Attend Medical Assistant School Full-Time


Choosing a part-time program can be a good option if you're balancing work, family, or other commitments. However, if your goal is to complete your training as quickly as possible, a full-time program is typically the faster route. With a more focused schedule, you can move through coursework and hands-on training sooner and be ready to start your career more quickly.


### 5. Plan for Your Clinical Experience Early


Most medical assistant programs include an internship or externship where you get to put the lessons you’ve learned to work in a real-world setting. To be sure you’re ready for it, find out early when it occurs, what requirements you need to complete beforehand, and what your schedule may look like.


Depending on the school, clinical participation may require documentation or other prerequisites that take time to arrange. You may also need to plan around work, childcare, transportation, or other responsibilities, so you can complete the required hours as scheduled.


Talk with your school early in your program about what you need to do and when. The sooner you prepare for your clinical experience, the less likely an unfinished requirement or scheduling conflict is to delay your progress toward graduation.


### 6. Don’t Miss Your Medical Assistant Classes


Choosing a fast-paced Medical Assistant program only helps you finish quickly if you keep up with the schedule. Because career-focused programs cover a lot of material in a relatively short period, missing even one or two classes can mean missing important instruction and hands-on practice.


Treat school like you would a job: show up consistently, arrive on time, complete assignments on schedule, and ask for help before you fall behind. Medical assistant training includes skills that are best learned through practice, so make attendance a priority so you stay on track toward completing your program on time.


Before enrolling, consider how school will fit with your work, transportation, childcare, and other responsibilities. Plan for those challenges in advance to make it easier to maintain consistent attendance once training begins.


### 7. Consider Where Certifications Fit In


Certification requirements for medical assistants vary by state and employer, so you should research the requirements where you plan to work. Find out how your program prepares you for certification exams like the Registered Medical Assistant (RMA) examination offered by[American Medical Technologists (AMT)](https://americanmedtech.org/medical-assistant) . Completing your program and meeting eligibility requirements does not guarantee certification; you must successfully complete the full certification process.


## Is Medical Assistant Training Right for Me?


The speed of a training program matters, but it shouldn't be the only factor you consider. Ask yourself what you want from your next career. Do you enjoy helping people? Are you comfortable interacting with patients? Can you stay organized while handling multiple responsibilities? Do you want a role where you can combine technical skills with communication and customer service? Medical assisting may be worth exploring.


## Start Training for a Medical Assistant Career


You don't need to spend years preparing for a career in healthcare. At Lincoln Tech, Medical Assistant training at several campuses can be completed in approximately 37 weeks, giving you the opportunity to build clinical, administrative, and professional skills in less than a year.
